outcomes: Explain UTF-8 byte sequences without conflating bytes and characters
Encode and decode arbitrary bytes exactly
Serialize merge order and reject malformed tokenizer files

utf-8.name: UTF-8
utf-8.definition: A variable-length Unicode encoding using one to four bytes per scalar value.
utf-8.explanation: UTF-8 preserves ASCII byte values and represents other Unicode scalar values with multi-byte sequences. Rust strings guarantee valid UTF-8, but a byte vector may contain incomplete or invalid sequences. Token boundaries in byte BPE can split a multi-byte character, so decoding each token independently as text is unsafe. Concatenate token bytes first and validate the complete result when a text boundary requires it. Byte counts and character counts therefore answer different questions and should always be labeled.

byte-pair-encoding.name: byte-pair encoding
byte-pair-encoding.definition: A tokenizer learned by repeatedly replacing frequent adjacent symbol pairs with new symbols.
byte-pair-encoding.explanation: Byte BPE starts with 256 symbols, one for every byte, and records an ordered list of merge rules. Each new token represents the concatenation of two earlier tokens. Encoding begins from bytes and applies rules by learned rank; decoding concatenates stored byte strings. The byte base guarantees coverage and exact round trips. Vocabulary size, merge order, tie-breaking, pre-tokenization, and normalization are all part of tokenizer identity because changing them can change token IDs consumed by a model.

round-trip.name: round trip
round-trip.definition: The invariant that decoding an encoded byte sequence reproduces the original bytes exactly.
round-trip.explanation: A round-trip test compares bytes rather than displayed strings: decode(encode(input)) must equal input. It catches overlapping replacements, incorrect learned-token bytes, invalid IDs, and serialization-order mistakes. Multilingual examples are valuable because UTF-8 characters span different byte lengths and token boundaries may split them. Exact round trip establishes reversibility, not compression quality or model accuracy. A reloaded tokenizer should satisfy the same invariant and produce identical token IDs when deterministic compatibility matters.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

checks: Multilingual byte round trips pass for ASCII, accented text, CJK, and emoji
Saved and reloaded merge tables are equal
Malformed headers and forward references return errors
Starter prints UTF-8 unit counts before its guided test
limitations: The teaching tokenizer omits production pre-tokenization
The text serialization has no checksum
